claims.text: Adding 0.5–1 wt% nano-sized Y2O3 to a WMoTaNbV-based refractory HEA will improve its yield strength relative to an undoped alloy.
Adding 0.5–1 wt% nano-sized Y2O3 to a WMoTaNbV-based refractory HEA will improve its creep resistance relative to an undoped alloy.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will maintain thermal stability under high-temperature exposure.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will maintain stability under irradiation.
Rigorous mechanical milling will produce a homogeneous dispersion of nano-sized Y2O3 particles in the alloy powder.
Mechanical milling followed by spark plasma sintering will yield uniformly dispersed Y2O3 nanoprecipitates embedded in the HEA matrix.
The Y2O3 nanoprecipitates will remain thermally stable in the HEA matrix.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles obstruct dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by Y2O3 nanoparticles enhances mechanical strength.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
The defect-sink behavior of Y2O3 nanoparticles enhances defect recombination during irradiation.
The high melting point of Y2O3 ensures thermal stability under the proposed extreme conditions.
The modified alloy's microstructure will remain stable during prolonged high-temperature irradiation.
An undoped WMoTaNbV refractory HEA typically has lower mechanical performance than the proposed oxide-dispersion-strengthened alloy under comparable conditions.
An undoped WMoTaNbV refractory HEA typically has lower creep resistance than the proposed oxide-dispersion-strengthened alloy under comparable conditions.
The predicted benefits depend on maintaining a uniform oxide dispersion and optimized processing conditions.
Nanoparticle distribution and interfacial bonding can influence the magnitude of the mechanical improvement.
